title: Datum — Parametric Sketch Solver
description: An interactive geometric constraint solver in the spirit of Sutherland's Sketchpad. Sketch points, lines and circles, then pin them together with real relations — coincident, horizontal/vertical, parallel, perpendicular, equal, tangent, concentric, point-on-line/circle, symmetric, colinear, midpoint, plus dimensional distance / angle / radius / diameter. Every relation becomes a scalar residual equation and the whole system is driven to zero by a from-scratch Levenberg–Marquardt least-squares solver. The Jacobian is EXACT: each residual is written once over an abstract arithmetic and re-run through a sparse forward-mode dual number, so the derivative is the residual code differentiated by the compiler — one source of truth, no finite-difference noise (a live differential test confirms it matches central differences to ~1e-9 across all 19 constraint kinds). Drag any point and the sketch re-solves live under your cursor; a Jacobian-rank degree-of-freedom analysis reports in real time whether the sketch is under-, well-, or over-constrained, and conflict diagnosis row-reduces the Jacobian to flag the SPECIFIC redundant constraints in red. One-click auto-constrain infers horizontal/vertical/parallel/perpendicular/equal/coincident from a rough drawing — admitting each only if it raises the rank, so it never over-constrains. Full undo/redo, save/open as JSON, and a shareable URL that reconstructs the whole sketch; double-click any dimension to retarget it. Eight worked examples DRIVE live, including the Peaucellier–Lipkin inversor (1864) that traces a mathematically EXACT straight line (held to ~1e-12 across its sweep) and Hoeken's approximate four-bar for contrast. A 17-check live self-test suite re-derives every claim from an independent reference.
